links.comparator_used: Varied prompt architectures requesting a grade level, judged against the requested reading grade level at baseline
links.outcome: Proportion of outputs initially meeting the requested reading grade level (RGL)
links.effect: Prompt architectures varied in how well they reached the desired RGL; few prompts reached the requested RGL at baseline. No numbers given in the abstract.
links.tradeoff: Prompting alone was unreliable, so 36 outputs per condition had to be generated and selected from.
links.quote: Prompt architectures varied in how well they initially resulted in a desired RGL, and few prompts resulted in requested RGLs at baseline.

links.comparator_used: Unselected baseline LLM outputs from prompting alone, with no readability scoring or selection
links.outcome: Median reading grade level of final outputs compared with the target grade bands
links.effect: Median RGLs were 5.8 (5.4-6.4) for level 1, 7.5 (7.4-7.7) for level 2, 9.5 (9.4-9.7) for level 3, and 11.5 (11.3-11.7) for level 4.
links.tradeoff: Required generating 36 explanations per condition, calculating RGLs for each, and then selecting outputs.
links.quote: After output selection and accuracy edits, median RGLs were 5.8 (5.4-6.4) for level 1, 7.5 (7.4-7.7) for level 2, 9.5 (9.4-9.7) for level 3, and 11.5 (11.3-11.7) for level 4.

links.comparator_used: Unreviewed LLM-generated text, with no head-to-head comparison; the study measured how many edits expert review required
links.outcome: Proportion of outputs needing clinician accuracy or completeness edits (word additions or deletions)
links.effect: 93.5%, 95.5%, 95.5%, and 95.0% of outputs for levels 1 through 4 needed no word additions or deletions, so roughly 4.5-6.5% were modified.
links.tradeoff: Three full professors had to review outputs in their specialties. Review burden was not quantified.
links.quote: Accuracy edits were minimal, with 93.5%, 95.5%, 95.5%, and 95.0% of outputs requiring no word additions or deletions for levels 1 through 4, respectively.

design_hint: reading-level constraints with output selection and expert review
